entries.name: Hill muscle force-velocity characteristic relation
entries.formula: (P + a)(V + b) = (P0 + a)b; equivalently V = b(P0 - P)/(P + a)
assumptions: Steady isotonic concentric shortening
Tetanic activation and approximately constant load during the measured shortening interval
Force and velocity refer to the contractile element under the stated series-elastic assumptions
Parameters a and b are positive and specific to the muscle preparation/condition

P0.meaning: Isometric force at zero shortening velocity

b.unit: m s^-1 or muscle lengths s^-1

validity.source_location: Hill (1938), Proc. R. Soc. B 126, 136-195; characteristic relation, cited source mapping pp. 174-177
validity.regime: Steady force-velocity relation during isotonic concentric shortening
limitations: Do not treat the normalized Hill force-velocity relation as the Hill ligand-binding equation
The rectangular hyperbola is empirical and does not fit all force/velocity extremes or all muscle preparations
Freeze force/velocity sign convention, muscle type, temperature and activation protocol before benchmarking
No algebraic rearrangement or parameter rescaling is a separate equation

review_notes: Primary source record and characteristic equation lineage identified

Exact page image transcription should be checked against the Royal Society original before source_verified status

Proposed only; not scientifically accepted or eligible for shard planning

entries.name: Poiseuille laminar tube-flow relation
entries.formula: Q = (p2 - p1) pi r^4 / (8 eta l)
assumptions: Steady laminar flow through a straight cylindrical tube
Incompressible Newtonian fluid with constant dynamic viscosity
No-slip at the tube wall and fully developed parabolic velocity profile
Rigid tube with constant radius and length
Pressure difference is measured between tube ends and flow is driven from higher to lower pressure

validity.source_location: OpenStax University Physics Volume 1 §14.7, Eq. 14.19; Poiseuille law for laminar flow
validity.regime: Laminar viscous flow through a cylindrical tube
limitations: Equation 14.18 defines hydraulic resistance; Eq. 14.19 combines it with Q=DeltaP/R and is the Poiseuille flow relation
Do not count resistance relation or algebraic rearrangements as separate equations
Not valid for turbulent flow, non-Newtonian fluids, significant entrance effects or compliant/noncylindrical conduits without model changes
Check Reynolds number and physical geometry for every generated sample

review_notes: Exact equation and section location are visible in OpenStax §14.7, Eq. 14.19
The source explicitly identifies incompressible laminar flow through a tube; figure caption describes viscosity and cylindrical geometry
Benchmark ranges must enforce p2>p1, positive r, eta and l, and a laminar Reynolds-number constraint
Train/extrapolation ranges and deterministic generator remain pending
Proposed only; not scientifically accepted or eligible for shard planning

entries.name: Planck blackbody spectral intensity law
entries.formula: I(lambda,T) = 2 pi h c^2 / [lambda^5 (exp(h c/(lambda kB T)) - 1)]
assumptions: Ideal blackbody/cavity radiation in thermal equilibrium
Spectral intensity is expressed per unit wavelength, not per unit frequency
Wavelength is positive and absolute temperature is positive
The emitter is treated as a blackbody; real-material emissivity deviations are outside this formula

validity.source_location: OpenStax University Physics Volume 3 §6.1, Eq. 6.11; Planck (1901), Annalen der Physik 309, 553-563, Eq. (8) is the primary historical source in the original spectral-distribution convention
validity.regime: Blackbody spectral power intensity per unit wavelength at thermal equilibrium
limitations: Do not confuse spectral intensity per wavelength with spectral energy density or frequency-domain forms; conversions require the correct Jacobian
Wien displacement and Stefan total-power relations are derived from the spectrum and are not separate independent candidates in this source family
Do not treat a real surface with wavelength-dependent emissivity as an ideal blackbody without adding emissivity
The original Planck paper uses a different spectral convention; this record selects the OpenStax wavelength-intensity convention explicitly

generator.output_units: W m^-3 (power per area per unit wavelength)

review_notes: Exact modern wavelength-intensity equation is visible as OpenStax Eq. 6.11
Primary Planck 1901 source is registered but uses a different original spectral-distribution convention; verify original Eq. (8) before source_verified status
Use physical constants with fixed SI values; sample only lambda and T in the benchmark adapter, not constants as independent random variables
Planck spectrum is the parent family for Wien maximum and Stefan integral; do not count those derived laws independently without a separate sampling design
Proposed only; not scientifically accepted or eligible for shard planning

assumptions: Paraxial ray approximation and thin-lens limit
Object and image distances are measured from the lens plane using the source sign convention
Lens is in a uniform surrounding medium and focal length is defined for that medium

do.meaning: Signed object distance; positive for a real object in the source convention

f.meaning: Signed focal length; positive for converging lens and negative for diverging lens

limitations: Image distance is signed; di>0 denotes a real image on the opposite side and di<0 a virtual image on the object side

entries.formula: V = B1^w1 * B2^w2 * B3^w3, with w1+w2+w3=1
assumptions: Three-token weighted pool with strictly positive normalized weights
Weights sum to one
All balances are expressed in consistent normalized/upscaled units

Do not treat algebraic rearrangements, unit conversions, parameter changes, or variable renamings as structurally distinct.
Protocol formulas must be version-tagged; Aave V3/V4 and Uniswap V2/V3/V4 mechanics are not interchangeable.
No calibration-ready independence claim is made by this manifest.
